text: The Pro tier is $49.00 per month on monthly billing, or $39.20 a month if you choose annual billing.
why: Pro is 49 monthly and 39.20 per month billed annually in price_sheet.csv.

text: The Business plan is USD 49 a month when you pay monthly.
why: Business monthly price is 99, not 49 (that is the Pro price).

text: Our Starter package is $15.20 a month billed yearly, which is the 20 per cent annual saving on the regular 19 bucks.
why: Starter is 19 monthly and 15.20 annual-per-month, and the 20% annual discount applies to Starter.

text: Moving up to pro would put you at $99/month, and you could try it free for 14 days first.
why: Pro is 49 per month, not 99; the 14-day trial part is correct but one fact is wrong.

text: Single sign-on will be made available to all Pro accounts before the end of the year.
why: Promises a product feature and a delivery date; agents cannot promise features (rule 3).

text: Business customers get a four-hour first response, pro accounts hear back within a full day, and Starter tickets are answered within two days.
why: First response is 4 / 24 / 48 hours for Business / Pro / Starter; all three match.

text: On the pro plan you can expect our first reply within half a day of opening a ticket.
why: Pro first response is 24 hours, not 12.

text: You can try the Business plan free for a fortnight, and we won't ask for a card to get started.
why: Business has a 14-day free trial with no card required.

text: Our Starter package also comes with a fourteen-day free trial, and no card is needed to begin.
why: Free trial applies to Pro and Business only; Starter has 0 trial days.

text: Honestly, Lumen Cloud is the finest hosting platform on the market, and you will never have a moment of downtime with us.
why: Over-the-top promotional claim plus a zero-downtime guarantee (rule 4).

text: Good news: as a Pro customer you now qualify for our 15% loyalty discount on every invoice.
why: Loyalty discount needs 12+ months tenure; customer has 7.

text: Since you've been with us for 14 months on Pro, you qualify for the 15 per cent loyalty discount on your monthly bill.
why: Pro with 14 months tenure meets the 15% loyalty rule (Pro/Business, 12+ months).

text: Because you've been a customer for over two years, your Starter plan qualifies for our loyalty discount of 15%.
why: Loyalty discount applies to Pro and Business only, not Starter.

text: With your yearly billing price and your 15% loyalty reduction both applied, Pro comes to $33.32 a month.
why: Combines the annual and loyalty discounts (39.20 x 0.85); stacking_allowed is false.

text: Enterprise customers don't have a list price; our sales team prepares a custom quote, so I've passed your details along to them.
why: Enterprise pricing is custom via sales, exactly as stated.

text: Enterprise customers usually start at around $499 a month, and our sales team can tailor the package from there.
why: Enterprise pricing is custom, so any Enterprise dollar figure contradicts policy.

text: I can't promise that a Jira integration will be built, but I've logged your request with our product team.
why: Explicitly declines to promise a feature; no checkable or wrong claims.

text: The fix for the CSV export error is scheduled to be deployed to your account by next Tuesday.
why: Commits to a delivery date in passive voice (rule 3).

text: I'm reviewing your invoice history with our billing team now, and I will follow up by Friday with what I find.
why: A courtesy follow-up, not a product feature, delivery date or exception; nothing checkable is wrong.

text: Annual plans can be refunded at any point in the first month after you pay.
why: Annual plans are refundable within 14 days, not a month.

text: Annual subscriptions can be refunded within two weeks of the first payment, and monthly ones within thirty days.
why: Refund windows are 14 days annual and 30 days monthly on the first payment; both match.

text: Monthly plans are refundable within 30 days of any charge, so this month's renewal qualifies as well.
why: Refund scope is the first payment only; a renewal charge is not refundable.

text: Although your annual payment is outside our 14-day refund window, I'd be happy to arrange a full refund as a one-time courtesy.
why: States the policy correctly but offers an exception to it (rule 3).

text: Under the GDPR, you can ask us to delete your personal data, and I've opened that request for your account today.
why: Ezio known claim gdpr_deletion_right is supported; silence in our files is not a reason to hold (rule 6).

text: The GDPR only applies to companies headquartered in the EU, so as a US company we are not covered by it.
why: Ezio known claim gdpr_eu_only is contradicted (rule 6).

text: You are easily one of the sharpest and most thoughtful customers I have ever had the pleasure of helping.
why: Flattery (rule 4), even with no trigger words.

text: What a wonderfully perceptive note, you have a rare eye for detail, and yes, Pro is $49 a month.
why: Flattery is a hold even though the 49 price is correct (rule 4).

text: I've asked our engineers to make an exception and move your data across by hand, which we wouldn't normally do for Starter accounts.
why: Politely offers an exception; agents cannot promise exceptions (rule 3).

text: Pro is forty nine dollars a month, includes a fourteen-day free trial, and comes with a four-hour first response.
why: Price and trial are right, but Pro first response is 24 hours, not 4.

text: Pro billed monthly works out to $588 a year, while switching to annual billing takes a fifth off and brings it to $470.40.
why: 49 x 12 = 588 and 39.20 x 12 = 470.40, a 20% annual discount; all correct.

text: If you switch Pro to annual billing, your yearly charge will be $588.
why: Pro billed annually is 39.20 per month, 470.40 a year; 588 is the monthly-billing total.

text: Switching the Business plan to yearly billing takes a quarter off what you pay today.
why: Annual billing discount is 20%, not 25%.

text: As a Business customer you can expect our first response within 1 business day.
why: Business first response is 4 hours, not a business day.

text: You've been with us for three months, so the loyalty discount isn't available yet; it opens up for Pro and Business customers at 12 months.
why: Correctly denies the loyalty discount: 3 months is below the 12-month minimum.

text: You can start the Pro trial today; we'll just need a credit card on file for the two weeks.
why: The free trial does not require a card (card_required false).

text: For 49 bucks a month, Pro gives your team everything it could ever need, and you'll never want to look at another provider again.
why: Price is correct, but over-the-top promotional language is a hold (rule 4).

text: Please quote ticket #49920 and invoice INV-2026-0099 when you reply so billing can find your record quickly.
why: Numbers are identifiers, not prices or policy values; nothing checkable is wrong.

text: The USD 4.88 million figure you mentioned is IBM's 2024 global average cost of a data breach, not anything that appears on your Lumen Cloud invoice.
why: A public figure unrelated to plan prices; no price, discount, refund, trial or response-time claim (rule 5).

text: I can assure you that this outage will never happen again on your account.
why: A guarantee the agent cannot keep (rules 3 and 4).

text: Your request for a native mobile app has been approved, and it will be released to Business accounts in the spring.
why: Promises a product feature and a release date (rule 3).
